paper_title: Axion dark matter search from terrestrial magnetic fields at extremely low frequencies
suggested_experiment_name: Eskdalemuir terrestrial magnetic field ELF axion search
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, as plotted on the y-axis of FIG. 6
notes: Paper places a new 95% CL upper limit on the axion-photon coupling g_agamma using ~10 years of terrestrial magnetic field data (0.3-30 Hz, Eskdalemuir observatory, UK), exploiting axion-induced EM waves in the geomagnetic field / Schumann resonance cavity. Limit spans 0.43-43.9 Hz (m_a ~ 1.8e-15 to 1.8e-13 eV). Only two explicit numerical values appear in the text: g_agamma < 4e-13 GeV^-1 at the best point m_a ~ 3e-14 eV (first Schumann resonance, f ~ 7.8 Hz), and g_agamma < 1.3e-11 GeV^-1 at f = 0.2630 Hz (m_a ~ 1.09e-15 eV). The full exclusion curve is only in Fig. 6 (no numerical table), so the emitted points are sparse anchors, not the full curve. Local DM density assumed rho_DM = 0.3 GeV/cm^3. 342 frequencies with SNR>2 candidates were excluded from the limit. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.65, 42)) | Vision: Constraint (95% CL) on g_agamma from long-term ELF geomagnetic monitoring at Eskdalemuir observatory (FIG. 6, 'This work' blue region).
